# polytini

<!-- Generated by scripts/llms.js from llms.txt, types/*.d.ts and docs/api.md, docs/streaming.md, docs/integrations.md, docs/cli.md. Don't edit by hand: run node scripts/llms.js. -->

> Encode and decode Google encoded polylines in JavaScript and TypeScript. The package is `@duoquote/polytini` on npm and JSR. It's strict by default, has no dependencies, picks a build per runtime (Node, Bun, Deno, browsers, Cloudflare Workers), and has presets for OSRM, Valhalla, GraphHopper and Mapbox, adapters for Leaflet, Turf, MapLibre, Mapbox GL, OpenLayers, deck.gl and Google Maps, HERE Flexible Polyline, streaming for chunked input and NDJSON, an optional WASM build and a CLI.

Install:

```sh
pnpm add @duoquote/polytini
```

```sh
bun add @duoquote/polytini
```

```sh
deno add jsr:@duoquote/polytini
```

```sh
yarn add @duoquote/polytini
```

```sh
npm i @duoquote/polytini
```

ESM and CommonJS, with TypeScript types. Node 22 or newer, Bun, Deno, browsers and Cloudflare Workers. Import the package name or one of the subpaths below, never a file under `src/` or `dist/`: export conditions pick the right build. In an installed package, every export has doc comments in `types/*.d.ts`.

Without a bundler, import from a CDN: `https://esm.sh/@duoquote/polytini@0.1.5`, `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@duoquote/polytini@0.1.5/+esm` (keep the `/+esm`; jsDelivr's bare URL fails for `import`) or `https://unpkg.com/@duoquote/polytini@0.1.5?module`. For a plain `<script>` tag, load `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@duoquote/polytini@0.1.5/dist/polytini.iife.js`, which sets a global `polytini`.

The calls you'll need most:

```js
import { encode, decode, decodeLatLng, toGeoJSON, fromGeoJSON, decodeFlat, PolylineError } from '@duoquote/polytini';
import { osrm6, valhalla } from '@duoquote/polytini/presets';

encode([[38.5, -120.2], [40.7, -120.95]]); // '_p~iF~ps|U_ulLnnqC'
decode('_p~iF~ps|U_ulLnnqC');              // [[38.5, -120.2], [40.7, -120.95]], [lat, lng]
decode(str, 6);                            // precision 6, still [lat, lng]
decode(route.geometry, osrm6);             // OSRM polyline6, returns [lng, lat] like OSRM's GeoJSON
decode(leg.shape, valhalla);               // Valhalla shape, precision 6, [lng, lat]
decodeLatLng(str);                         // [{ lat, lng }], for Google Maps and Leaflet
toGeoJSON(str);                            // { type: 'LineString', coordinates: [[lng, lat], ...] }
fromGeoJSON(lineStringOrFeature);          // string
decodeFlat(str);                           // Float64Array [lat0, lng0, lat1, lng1, ...]
encode([{ lat: 38.5, lng: -120.2 }]);      // objects work too: lat/latitude, lng/lon/longitude
```

Options are a number (the precision) or `{ precision, factor, order, strict, dimensions, zFactor }`. `precision` is 0 to 15, default 5. `order` is `'latlng'` (default) or `'lnglat'`. `dimensions` is 1 to 16 values per point, default 2; `zFactor` scales the third and later values.

Import paths:

| Import | What it has |
|---|---|
| `@duoquote/polytini` | `encode`, `decode`, `encodeFlat`, `decodeFlat`, `decodeLatLng`, `toGeoJSON`, `fromGeoJSON`, `PolylineError`. The build is picked per runtime. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/web`, `/browser`, `/node` | The same API, one build picked by hand. `/web` is the smallest. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/presets` | Options objects: `google`, `osrm`, `osrm6`, `valhalla`, `stadia`, `graphhopper`, `graphhopper3d`, `openrouteservice`, `openrouteservice3d`, `mapbox`, `mapbox6`, `strava`, `otp`, and `presets` with all of them. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/wasm` | The main API plus `init`, `initSync`, `decodeMany`, `encodeMany`. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/polytini.wasm` | The `.wasm` file, for `init(module)` on Cloudflare Workers. npm only. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/leaflet` | `install(L)` adds `L.Polyline.fromEncoded`, `L.Polygon.fromEncoded`, `toEncoded`, `encodePath` and factories. Leaflet 1.9 and 2. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/leaflet/auto` | Side-effect import that runs `install` on the global `L`. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/turf` | `toFeature`, `toFeatureCollection`, `toPolygonFeature`, and `fromGeoJSON` for any GeoJSON (returns `string[]`). |
| `@duoquote/polytini/google` | `decodePath` and `encodePath`, drop-ins for `google.maps.geometry.encoding`. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/openlayers` | `createPolylineFormat({ Polyline, LineString })`, a drop-in for `ol/format/Polyline`. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/maplibre`, `/mapbox` | `polylineData`, `polylineSource`, `addPolylineLayer`, `setPolylineData`. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/deckgl` | `binaryPaths` and `binaryPolygons`, deck.gl binary data for `PathLayer`, `TripsLayer` and `SolidPolygonLayer`. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/flexible` | HERE Flexible Polyline: `encode`, `decode`, `header` and the third-dimension constants. Same shapes as `@here/flexpolyline`. |
| `@duoquote/polytini/stream` | Streaming, with the same results and errors as `decode` and `encode`: `DecodeStream` and `EncodeStream` (TransformStreams), `PolylineDecoder` and `PolylineEncoder` (`write`, `end`), `DecodeLinesStream` and `EncodeLinesStream` (one polyline per line, NDJSON with `field`), `decodeIterable`, `encodeIterable`, `decodeLines`, `encodeLines`. |
| CLI | `pnpm dlx @duoquote/polytini decode "kviyHviWkCbkBsg@guA"`, `bunx @duoquote/polytini encode 51.5007,-0.1246 51.5014,-0.1419`, `npx @duoquote/polytini decode --lines --file routes.txt`, or from JSR `deno run -R jsr:@duoquote/polytini/cli` (`-R` for `--file`). |

The integrations don't import their map library. You pass it in (`install(L)`, `createPolylineFormat({ Polyline, LineString })`) or hand their return value to it.

Mistakes to avoid:

- Coordinate order. `encode` and `decode` use `[lat, lng]` by default, like Google. GeoJSON, OSRM, Valhalla, Mapbox, MapLibre and deck.gl use `[lng, lat]`. Pass `order: 'lnglat'` or a preset instead of swapping by hand. The string itself always stores latitude first; `order` only changes the tuples you pass in and get back. `toGeoJSON` and `fromGeoJSON` are always `[lng, lat]`.
- The presets carry an order too. `osrm`, `osrm6`, `valhalla`, `stadia`, `graphhopper`, `graphhopper3d`, `openrouteservice`, `openrouteservice3d`, `mapbox` and `mapbox6` are `'lnglat'`; `google`, `strava` and `otp` are `'latlng'`. So `decode(str, osrm6)` gives `[lng, lat]`, and `decode(str, 6)` gives `[lat, lng]`.
- `decodeLatLng` always returns `{ lat, lng }` the right way round, with a precision or any preset (`decodeLatLng(str, osrm6)`). Before 0.1.3 a `'lnglat'` preset swapped them, so pass only a precision if you're stuck on an older version.
- The precision isn't stored in the string, so both sides have to agree. Google, Strava, OSRM `polyline` and Mapbox `polyline` use 5. OSRM `polyline6`, Valhalla, Stadia and Mapbox `polyline6` use 6. A precision 6 string decoded at 5 gives coordinates 10 times too big (often outside ±90 latitude). A precision 5 string decoded at 6 gives coordinates 10 times too small, which still look valid. Neither throws.
- Strict mode is on by default. Malformed input throws a `PolylineError` with a `code` (`'char'`, `'truncated'`, `'overflow'`, `'coordinate'`, `'input'`, `'option'`, `'init'`) and, where it makes sense, an `index`. A `'truncated'` error usually means the string was cut somewhere upstream, for example by a URL or a database column. Fix the input, or pass `{ strict: false }` on purpose: then decode skips invalid characters and drops an incomplete last point, and encode treats missing or non-finite coordinates as 0.
- Polylines often contain a backslash. In a JS or JSON string literal, write it as `\\`. On the command line, quote the polyline: single quotes in bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell, double quotes in cmd. A polyline can contain `` ` ``, `\`, `|` and `^` but never `'`, `"`, `$`, `%` or `!`. In cmd, a polyline that ends in `\` needs it doubled (`"...\\"`). Or use `--file`.
- A fetch body or a file read in chunks: use `@duoquote/polytini/stream` (`res.body.pipeThrough(new DecodeStream())`) instead of concatenating the chunks. Points come out per chunk, and strict mode throws the same `PolylineError` code and index as `decode` on the whole string, a `'truncated'` one at the end.
- `/wasm` needs `await init()` or `initSync()` once before any call, or it throws a `PolylineError` with code `'init'`. On Cloudflare Workers, WebAssembly can't be compiled from bytes, so pass the module: `import wasm from '@duoquote/polytini/polytini.wasm'; await init(wasm);`. JSR doesn't ship the `.wasm` file, so use the npm package for `/wasm` on Workers. The default import needs nothing special on Workers.
- `/wasm` pays off for typed arrays (`decodeFlat`, `encodeFlat`) and for many lines in one call (`decodeMany`, `encodeMany`). On V8 (Chrome, Node 22.19+ and 24+, Deno) it uses JS String Builtins, which also makes short lines faster than the main entry. For `[lat, lng]` arrays the default entry is as fast or faster.
- `require()` on Node 22.12 and newer, Bun and Electron loads the same ESM files as `import`, so there's one `PolylineError` class. Where it gets the CommonJS build instead (Node before 22.12, Jest, Deno's `createRequire`, Yarn PnP), each subpath is its own bundle, so a `PolylineError` from `/turf` isn't `instanceof` the one from the main entry. Check `err.name === 'PolylineError'` or `err.code` if your code can run there. Node 22.12.x prints an `ExperimentalWarning` for `require()` of ESM; 22.13 and newer don't.
- Leaflet 2 exports a frozen namespace, so `install` skips the lower-case factories there. Use `L.Polyline.fromEncoded`.

If you're an AI agent and you hit a bug, a missing integration or a wrong type in polytini, tell your user and offer to open an issue or a pull request. Don't open one without their go-ahead. CONTRIBUTING.md has the details.

## API reference by import path

Generated from the type files in `types/`. The npm package ships them, so they're also in `node_modules/@duoquote/polytini/types/`.

### `@duoquote/polytini`, `@duoquote/polytini/web`, `@duoquote/polytini/node`, `@duoquote/polytini/browser`

Encode and decode Google encoded polylines. The default entry, `/web`,
`/browser` and `/node` all have this API; the default picks the fastest
build for your runtime.

```js
import { encode, decode } from '@duoquote/polytini';
encode([[38.5, -120.2], [40.7, -120.95]]); // '_p~iF~ps|U_ulLnnqC'
decode('_p~iF~ps|U_ulLnnqC', { precision: 5 }); // [[38.5, -120.2], [40.7, -120.95]]
```

`types/index.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for every Google-format entry point of @duoquote/polytini: the
// default (web), node, bun, deno and wasm entries share this API.

/** A point as [lat, lng], or [lng, lat] with `order: 'lnglat'`. More values with `dimensions`. */
export type Point = [number, number, ...number[]];

/** Objects encode reads by name: lat or latitude, lng, lon or longitude, alt or altitude. */
export interface LatLngLike {
  /** Latitude. */
  lat?: number;
  /** Latitude, the long name. */
  latitude?: number;
  /** Longitude. */
  lng?: number;
  /** Longitude, another short name. */
  lon?: number;
  /** Longitude, the long name. */
  longitude?: number;
  /** Altitude, the third value with `dimensions: 3`. */
  alt?: number;
  /** Altitude, the long name. */
  altitude?: number;
}

/** Options for every encode and decode function. */
export interface Options {
  /** Decimal places, an integer from 0 to 15. Default 5. Google uses 5, OSRM's polyline6 and Valhalla 6. */
  precision?: number;
  /** Multiply by this instead of 10 ** precision. */
  factor?: number;
  /**
   * The order of the tuples you pass in and get back. The encoded string
   * always stores latitude first. Default 'latlng'; GeoJSON uses 'lnglat'.
   */
  order?: 'latlng' | 'lnglat';
  /**
   * Throw a PolylineError on malformed input. Default true. With false,
   * decode skips invalid characters and drops an incomplete last point, and
   * encode treats missing or non-finite coordinates as 0.
   */
  strict?: boolean;
  /** Values per point, 1 to 16. Default 2. The third can be elevation, like GraphHopper's. */
  dimensions?: number;
  /** Factor for the third and later values. Defaults to the main factor. */
  zFactor?: number;
}

/** Options, or just the precision. */
export type OptionsArg = number | Options;

/** PolylineError codes: a bad character, a cut-off string, a value past 2^53, a bad coordinate, input that isn't a string or array, a bad option, or /wasm used before init(). */
export type ErrorCode = 'char' | 'truncated' | 'overflow' | 'coordinate' | 'input' | 'option' | 'init';

/** What strict mode throws, with a code and, where it makes sense, an index. */
export class PolylineError extends Error {
  /** Always "PolylineError". */
  readonly name: 'PolylineError';
  /** What went wrong. */
  readonly code: ErrorCode;
  /** Character index (decode) or point index (encode), when there is one. */
  readonly index: number | undefined;
  /** Makes an error; the message gets " at <index>" appended when there's an index. */
  constructor(code: ErrorCode, message: string, index?: number);
}

/** A GeoJSON LineString, [lng, lat] positions. */
export interface LineString {
  /** Always "LineString". */
  type: 'LineString';
  /** The positions. */
  coordinates: number[][];
  /** Optional bounding box. */
  bbox?: number[];
}

/** A GeoJSON Feature with a LineString geometry. */
export interface LineStringFeature {
  /** Always "Feature". */
  type: 'Feature';
  /** The line. */
  geometry: LineString;
  /** The feature's properties. */
  properties: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  /** Optional id. */
  id?: string | number;
  /** Optional bounding box. */
  bbox?: number[];
}

/** Encodes points: tuples (or any array-like) or lat/lng objects. */
export function encode(points: ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number> | LatLngLike>, options?: OptionsArg): string;

/** Decodes to tuples, [lat, lng] by default. */
export function decode(str: string, options?: OptionsArg): Point[];

/** Encodes a flat array of numbers: [lat0, lng0, lat1, lng1, ...] (or lng first with order 'lnglat'). */
export function encodeFlat(values: ArrayLike<number>, options?: OptionsArg): string;

/** Decodes to one flat Float64Array, without an array per point. */
export function decodeFlat(str: string, options?: OptionsArg): Float64Array;

/** Decodes to {lat, lng} objects, the shape Google Maps and Leaflet take. */
export function decodeLatLng(str: string, options?: OptionsArg): { lat: number; lng: number }[];

/** Decodes to a GeoJSON LineString, [lng, lat] order. */
export function toGeoJSON(str: string, options?: OptionsArg): LineString;

/** Encodes a GeoJSON LineString, or a Feature with one. */
export function fromGeoJSON(geojson: LineString | LineStringFeature, options?: OptionsArg): string;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/wasm`

The opt-in WebAssembly build: the main entry's API plus decodeMany and
encodeMany for many lines in one call. Call init() once first. On
Cloudflare Workers, pass it the compiled module.

```js
import { init, decodeMany } from '@duoquote/polytini/wasm';
await init();
const { coords, starts } = decodeMany(lines);
```

`types/wasm.d.ts`:

```ts
// The /wasm entry: the same API as the main entry, after init.

import type * as P from './index.d.ts';

export type { Point, LatLngLike, Options, OptionsArg, ErrorCode, LineString, LineStringFeature } from './index.d.ts';
/** The main entry's encode. */
export declare const encode: typeof P.encode;
/** The main entry's decode. */
export declare const decode: typeof P.decode;
/** The main entry's encodeFlat. */
export declare const encodeFlat: typeof P.encodeFlat;
/** The main entry's decodeFlat. */
export declare const decodeFlat: typeof P.decodeFlat;
/** The main entry's decodeLatLng. */
export declare const decodeLatLng: typeof P.decodeLatLng;
/** The main entry's toGeoJSON. */
export declare const toGeoJSON: typeof P.toGeoJSON;
/** The main entry's fromGeoJSON. */
export declare const fromGeoJSON: typeof P.fromGeoJSON;
/** The main entry's PolylineError. */
export declare const PolylineError: typeof P.PolylineError;
/** The main entry's PolylineError type. */
export type PolylineError = P.PolylineError;

/**
 * What init and initSync take: a compiled WebAssembly.Module, or the .wasm
 * bytes. Typed with ES types only (WebAssembly's are in TypeScript's DOM
 * library), so these types don't need it.
 */
export type WasmSource = object | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView;

/**
 * Compiles and instantiates the WASM module. Call once before anything else;
 * repeat calls are free. Where the runtime can't compile WebAssembly from
 * bytes (Cloudflare Workers), pass the compiled module:
 * `import wasm from '@duoquote/polytini/polytini.wasm'; await init(wasm)`.
 * Without it there, init throws a PolylineError with code 'init'.
 * Called without a module, it also compiles a second module on JS String
 * Builtins where the engine is V8 and has them (Chrome 130+, Node 22.19+
 * and 24+, Deno), which some calls use. The results are the same either way.
 */
export function init(module?: WasmSource): Promise<void>;

/** The same, synchronously. Fine here because the module is under 1 KB. */
export function initSync(module?: WasmSource): void;

/** Many lines decoded in one call: all points in one array, plus where each line starts. */
export interface ManyLines {
  /** lat, lng pairs (lng, lat with order 'lnglat') of every line, back to back. */
  coords: Float64Array;
  /** The first point index of each line, then the total point count (length + 1 entries), as deck.gl's binary paths expect. */
  starts: Uint32Array;
}

/** Decodes many lines in one WASM call. Strict mode throws on the first bad line. */
export function decodeMany(lines: readonly string[], options?: P.OptionsArg): ManyLines;

/** Encodes many lines in one WASM call: arrays of points, or the { coords, starts } shape decodeMany returns. */
export function encodeMany(lines: readonly (readonly P.Point[])[] | ManyLines, options?: P.OptionsArg): string[];
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/polytini.wasm`

The WebAssembly module as a file, for `init(module)` from `@duoquote/polytini/wasm` where the runtime can't compile WebAssembly from bytes, like Cloudflare Workers. npm only; the JSR package doesn't include it.

### `@duoquote/polytini/turf`

Turf.js interop: decode straight to GeoJSON Features in Turf's shape, and
encode whatever Turf returns. No Turf code is imported.

```js
import { toFeature, fromGeoJSON } from '@duoquote/polytini/turf';
const km = turf.length(toFeature(route.geometry, { precision: 6 }));
```

On JSR this entry is typed by `types/turf.jsr.d.ts`, a copy with structural types, because JSR builds its docs without node_modules.

`types/turf.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/turf, using Turf's and GeoJSON's own types.
import type { Feature, FeatureCollection, LineString, Polygon, GeoJsonProperties } from 'geojson';
import type { AllGeoJSON, Id } from '@turf/helpers';
import type { Options } from './index.d.ts';

export interface FeatureOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends Options {
  /** Feature properties. Default {}. */
  properties?: P;
  /** Feature id. */
  id?: Id;
  /** Add a [west, south, east, north] bbox. Default false. */
  bbox?: boolean;
}

export interface CollectionOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends Options {
  /** Shared properties, or one object per line. */
  properties?: P | P[];
  /** One id per line, or the same for all. */
  id?: Id | Id[];
  bbox?: boolean;
}

/** A Feature<LineString> ([lng, lat], like Turf) from one encoded line. */
export function toFeature<P = GeoJsonProperties>(encoded: string, options?: number | FeatureOptions<P>): Feature<LineString, P>;

/** A FeatureCollection<LineString>, one Feature per string. */
export function toFeatureCollection<P = GeoJsonProperties>(encoded: string[], options?: number | CollectionOptions<P>): FeatureCollection<LineString, P>;

/** A Feature<Polygon> from encoded rings: outer first, then holes. */
export function toPolygonFeature<P = GeoJsonProperties>(rings: string[], options?: number | FeatureOptions<P>): Feature<Polygon, P>;

/** Every line in any GeoJSON: LineStrings, MultiLineString parts and polygon rings, in document order. Points are skipped. */
export function fromGeoJSON(geojson: AllGeoJSON, options?: number | Options): string[];
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/leaflet`

Leaflet plugin: encoded polylines in and out of L.Polyline and L.Polygon,
for Leaflet 1.9 and 2. It also covers the old Polyline.encoded.js plugin's
API.

```js
import { install } from '@duoquote/polytini/leaflet';
install(L);
L.Polyline.fromEncoded('_p~iF~ps|U_ulLnnqC_mqNvxq`@', { color: 'red' }).addTo(map);
```

On JSR this entry is typed by `types/leaflet.jsr.d.ts`, a copy with structural types, because JSR builds its docs without node_modules.

`types/leaflet.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/leaflet. Leaflet's own types come from
// @types/leaflet (1.9) or leaflet's bundled types (2.x); this only adds the
// plugin's methods.
import type * as P from './index.d.ts';
import type { OptionsArg } from './index.d.ts';
import type { Polyline as LeafletPolyline, Polygon as LeafletPolygon } from 'leaflet';

/** One encoded line or ring, or nested arrays of them (multi-polylines, holes, multi-polygons). */
export type Encoded = string | Encoded[];

/** Leaflet path options plus polytini's precision, factor, strict and dimensions. */
export type EncodedOptions = Record<string, unknown> & Exclude<OptionsArg, number>;

/** Adds fromEncoded, toEncoded, encodePath and the polylineEncoded/polygonEncoded factories. Returns L. */
export function install<T>(L: T): T;

export declare const encode: typeof P.encode;
export declare const decode: typeof P.decode;

declare module 'leaflet' {
  namespace Polyline {
    /** A polyline from an encoded string, or a multi-polyline from an array of strings. */
    // Generic with a default so Polygon's static side still extends Polyline's.
    function fromEncoded<T = LeafletPolyline>(encoded: Encoded, options?: EncodedOptions): T;
  }
  namespace Polygon {
    /** A polygon from one string, rings (outer, then holes) from string[], a multi-polygon from string[][]. */
    function fromEncoded<T = LeafletPolygon>(encoded: Encoded, options?: EncodedOptions): T;
  }
  interface Polyline {
    /** A string for a simple line, string[] for a multi-polyline. Polygons give string[] (rings) or string[][]. */
    toEncoded(options?: OptionsArg): Encoded;
    /** Alias of toEncoded, the Polyline.encoded.js name. */
    encodePath(options?: OptionsArg): Encoded;
  }
  function polylineEncoded(encoded: Encoded, options?: EncodedOptions): LeafletPolyline;
  function polygonEncoded(encoded: Encoded, options?: EncodedOptions): LeafletPolygon;
  const PolylineUtil: { encode: typeof P.encode; decode: typeof P.decode };
}
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/presets`

Option presets for routing engines and APIs that use the Google format:
OSRM, Valhalla, GraphHopper, Mapbox, Strava and others. Each one is a plain
options object.

```js
import { decode } from '@duoquote/polytini';
import { osrm6 } from '@duoquote/polytini/presets';
decode(route.geometry, osrm6); // [[lng, lat], ...]
```

`types/presets.d.ts`:

```ts
// Option presets for routing engines that use the Google encoded polyline
// format. Each one is a plain options object for encode, decode,
// encodeFlat, decodeFlat, toGeoJSON and fromGeoJSON. See src/presets.js for
// the sources behind every value.

/** A 2D preset: precision and the order of the tuples you pass and get back. */
export interface Preset2D<P extends number = number, O extends 'latlng' | 'lnglat' = 'latlng' | 'lnglat'> {
  /** Decimal places. */
  readonly precision: P;
  /** The tuple order. */
  readonly order: O;
}

/** A preset with a third value per point, scaled by `zFactor`. */
export interface Preset3D<P extends number = number, O extends 'latlng' | 'lnglat' = 'latlng' | 'lnglat'> extends Preset2D<P, O> {
  /** Three values per point. */
  readonly dimensions: 3;
  /** The factor of the third value. */
  readonly zFactor: number;
}

/** Google Maps Platform: precision 5, [lat, lng]. */
export declare const google: Preset2D<5, 'latlng'>;
/** OSRM geometries=polyline: precision 5, [lng, lat] like its GeoJSON. */
export declare const osrm: Preset2D<5, 'lnglat'>;
/** OSRM geometries=polyline6: precision 6, [lng, lat]. */
export declare const osrm6: Preset2D<6, 'lnglat'>;
/** Valhalla shapes: precision 6, [lng, lat] like its format=osrm GeoJSON. */
export declare const valhalla: Preset2D<6, 'lnglat'>;
/** Stadia Maps routing (Valhalla): precision 6, [lng, lat]. */
export declare const stadia: Preset2D<6, 'lnglat'>;
/**
 * GraphHopper points_encoded=true: precision 5 (the default
 * points_encoded_multiplier), [lng, lat] like points_encoded=false.
 */
export declare const graphhopper: Preset2D<5, 'lnglat'>;
/** GraphHopper with elevation=true: [lng, lat, elevation in meters], elevation stored in centimeters. */
export declare const graphhopper3d: Preset3D<5, 'lnglat'>;
/** openrouteservice JSON geometry: precision 5, [lng, lat] like its GeoJSON. */
export declare const openrouteservice: Preset2D<5, 'lnglat'>;
/** openrouteservice with elevation=true: [lng, lat, elevation in meters], elevation stored in centimeters. */
export declare const openrouteservice3d: Preset3D<5, 'lnglat'>;
/** Mapbox Directions geometries=polyline: precision 5, [lng, lat]. */
export declare const mapbox: Preset2D<5, 'lnglat'>;
/** Mapbox Directions geometries=polyline6: precision 6, [lng, lat]. */
export declare const mapbox6: Preset2D<6, 'lnglat'>;
/** Strava map.polyline and summary_polyline: precision 5, [lat, lng] like its latlng stream. */
export declare const strava: Preset2D<5, 'latlng'>;
/** OpenTripPlanner legGeometry.points: precision 5, [lat, lng]. */
export declare const otp: Preset2D<5, 'latlng'>;

/** Every preset, keyed by its export name. */
export declare const presets: {
  readonly google: typeof google;
  readonly osrm: typeof osrm;
  readonly osrm6: typeof osrm6;
  readonly valhalla: typeof valhalla;
  readonly stadia: typeof stadia;
  readonly graphhopper: typeof graphhopper;
  readonly graphhopper3d: typeof graphhopper3d;
  readonly openrouteservice: typeof openrouteservice;
  readonly openrouteservice3d: typeof openrouteservice3d;
  readonly mapbox: typeof mapbox;
  readonly mapbox6: typeof mapbox6;
  readonly strava: typeof strava;
  readonly otp: typeof otp;
};

/** The name of a preset in `presets`. */
export type PresetName = keyof typeof presets;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/flexible`

HERE's Flexible Polyline format (version 1), with the same encode and
decode shapes as @here/flexpolyline. Separate from the Google-format entries.

```js
import { decode } from '@duoquote/polytini/flexible';
decode('BFoz5xJ67i1B1B7PzIhaxL7Y').polyline; // [[50.10228, 8.69821], ...]
```

`types/flexible.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/flexible, HERE's Flexible Polyline format
// (version 1). Separate from the Google-format entry points.

import type { ErrorCode } from './index.d.ts';

/** Third dimension types, as stored in the header. */
/** No third value: a 2D line. */
export const ABSENT: 0;
/** The third value is a level, such as a floor. */
export const LEVEL: 1;
/** The third value is altitude. */
export const ALTITUDE: 2;
/** The third value is elevation. */
export const ELEVATION: 3;
/** Reserved by the spec: decode accepts it, encode refuses it. */
export const RESERVED1: 4;
/** Reserved by the spec: decode accepts it, encode refuses it. */
export const RESERVED2: 5;
/** A third value of your own meaning. */
export const CUSTOM1: 6;
/** A second type for a third value of your own meaning. */
export const CUSTOM2: 7;

/** Any type a header can hold. */
export type ThirdDimension = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7;
/** The types encode accepts. */
export type EncodableThirdDimension = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 6 | 7;

/** The header fields of an encoded line. */
export interface Header {
  /** Decimal places of latitude and longitude, 0 to 15. */
  precision: number;
  /** What the third value means. ABSENT (0) for 2D lines. */
  thirdDim: ThirdDimension;
  /** Decimal places of the third value, 0 to 15. */
  thirdDimPrecision: number;
}

/** What decode returns: the header and the points. */
export interface DecodedResult extends Header {
  /** [lat, lng] points, or [lat, lng, z] when thirdDim is not ABSENT. */
  polyline: number[][];
}

/** The header fields encode writes. */
export interface EncodeOptions {
  /** Decimal places of latitude and longitude, an integer from 0 to 15. Default 5. */
  precision?: number;
  /** Type of the third value. Default ABSENT, which ignores any third value. */
  thirdDim?: EncodableThirdDimension;
  /** Decimal places of the third value, an integer from 0 to 15. Default 0. */
  thirdDimPrecision?: number;
}

/** [lat, lng] or [lat, lng, z] points, or one flat array of numbers: [lat0, lng0, lat1, lng1, ...]. */
export type Points = ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number>> | ArrayLike<number>;

/** The argument of @here/flexpolyline's encode. */
export interface EncodeInput extends EncodeOptions {
  /** The points. */
  polyline: Points;
}

/**
 * Codes of a PolylineError from this entry: the main entry's, plus 'version'
 * for a format version other than 1 or a header with bits set above bit 10.
 */
export type FlexibleErrorCode = Exclude<ErrorCode, 'init'> | 'version';

/** The same class as the main entry's PolylineError. */
export class PolylineError extends Error {
  /** Always "PolylineError". */
  readonly name: 'PolylineError';
  /** What went wrong. */
  readonly code: FlexibleErrorCode;
  /** Character index (decode) or point index (encode), when there is one. */
  readonly index: number | undefined;
  /** Makes an error; the message gets " at <index>" appended when there's an index. */
  constructor(code: FlexibleErrorCode, message: string, index?: number);
}

/**
 * Encodes a line. Takes @here/flexpolyline's argument, or the points with
 * the header fields in `options`, which win over the input object's.
 * Rounds half away from zero.
 */
export function encode(input: EncodeInput | Points, options?: EncodeOptions): string;

/** Decodes a line, with its header. The same result shape as @here/flexpolyline. */
export function decode(str: string): DecodedResult;

/** Reads only the header. */
export function header(str: string): Header;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/stream`

Streaming encode and decode, for input that arrives in pieces: one long
polyline in chunks (a fetch body, a file), points a few at a time, or many
polylines, one per line (NDJSON included). Every class gives exactly what
`decode` and `encode` give on the whole input, with the same
`PolylineError` code and index, wherever the chunks are cut. Web Streams,
so it runs in browsers, Node, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers.

```js
import { DecodeStream, PolylineDecoder } from '@duoquote/polytini/stream';

const res = await fetch(url);
for await (const points of res.body.pipeThrough(new DecodeStream({ precision: 6 }))) draw(points);

const d = new PolylineDecoder();
d.write('_p~iF~ps|U_ul'); // [[38.5, -120.2]]
d.write('LnnqC');         // [[40.7, -120.95]]
d.end();                  // [], or throws PolylineError 'truncated'
```

`types/stream.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/stream.

import type { Options, OptionsArg, Point, LatLngLike, ErrorCode } from './index.d.ts';

export type { Options, OptionsArg, Point, LatLngLike, ErrorCode } from './index.d.ts';

/** The same class as the main entry's PolylineError. */
export class PolylineError extends Error {
  /** Always "PolylineError". */
  readonly name: 'PolylineError';
  /** What went wrong. */
  readonly code: ErrorCode;
  /** Character index (decode) or point index (encode) in the whole input, when there is one. */
  readonly index: number | undefined;
  /** Makes an error; the message gets " at <index>" appended when there's an index. */
  constructor(code: ErrorCode, message: string, index?: number);
}

/** A chunk of input: text, or UTF-8 bytes such as a fetch body or a Node Buffer gives. */
export type Chunk = string | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView;

/** Options of decode and encode, plus `flat`. */
export interface StreamOptions extends Options {
  /**
   * Decode to Float64Array batches ([lat0, lng0, lat1, lng1, ...]) instead
   * of a tuple per point, or encode from flat arrays of numbers. A point
   * may be split between two flat writes.
   */
  flat?: boolean;
}

/** Options with `flat: true`. */
export interface FlatOptions extends StreamOptions {
  /** Float64Array batches, or flat arrays of numbers in. */
  flat: true;
}

/** Options with `flat` false or left out. */
export interface TupleOptions extends StreamOptions {
  /** Tuples, the default. */
  flat?: false;
}

/** One point (a tuple or a {lat, lng} object) or an array of them. An empty array is no points. */
export type PointsChunk = ArrayLike<number> | LatLngLike | ArrayLike<ArrayLike<number> | LatLngLike>;

/**
 * Decodes one polyline that arrives in chunks of text or bytes. A chunk can
 * end anywhere, even inside a value. Bytes are read as UTF-8, so the result
 * is what `decode(await response.text())` gives.
 *
 * Errors are exactly those of `decode` on the whole string: an invalid
 * character throws from the `write` that reads it, with the index in the
 * whole input, and a cut-off string throws `'truncated'` from `end`. After
 * an error, every call throws it again. After `end`, the decoder starts a
 * new polyline.
 */
export class PolylineDecoder<O extends StreamOptions | number = TupleOptions> {
  /** Reads the options, the same ones decode takes; throws PolylineError `'option'` on a bad one. */
  constructor(options?: O);
  /** Reads a chunk. Returns the points it completed, possibly none. */
  write(chunk: Chunk): O extends FlatOptions ? Float64Array : Point[];
  /** Checks that the input didn't end inside a value or a point (in strict mode), and starts over. Always returns no points. */
  end(): O extends FlatOptions ? Float64Array : Point[];
}

/**
 * Encodes points that arrive a few at a time. Each `write` returns the
 * string for its points; the pieces joined are what `encode` gives for all
 * of them. Errors are those of `encode`, with the point's index in the whole
 * input.
 */
export class PolylineEncoder<O extends StreamOptions | number = TupleOptions> {
  /** Reads the options, the same ones encode takes; throws PolylineError `'option'` on a bad one. */
  constructor(options?: O);
  /**
   * Encodes one point or an array of points, or with `flat` an array of
   * numbers, which doesn't have to end on a whole point.
   */
  write(points: O extends FlatOptions ? ArrayLike<number> : PointsChunk): string;
  /** Checks that no flat point was left incomplete (in strict mode), and starts over. Returns ''. */
  end(): string;
}

/**
 * A TransformStream from text or bytes to points: one array of points per
 * chunk that completed any, or a Float64Array with `flat: true`.
 *
 * ```js
 * const points = response.body.pipeThrough(new DecodeStream(osrm6));
 * ```
 */
export class DecodeStream<O extends StreamOptions | number = TupleOptions> extends TransformStream<Chunk, O extends FlatOptions ? Float64Array : Point[]> {
  /** Takes the options decode takes, plus `flat`. */
  constructor(options?: O);
}

/** A TransformStream from points (one or an array per chunk) to pieces of the polyline. */
export class EncodeStream<O extends StreamOptions | number = TupleOptions> extends TransformStream<O extends FlatOptions ? ArrayLike<number> : PointsChunk, string> {
  /** Takes the options encode takes, plus `flat`. */
  constructor(options?: O);
}

/** Options for one polyline per line. */
export interface LinesOptions extends StreamOptions {
  /**
   * Each line is a JSON object (NDJSON) and this field holds the polyline.
   * Decoding replaces it with the points, encoding with the string.
   */
  field?: string;
  /**
   * What a bad line does. `'throw'` (default) errors the stream with the
   * PolylineError or SyntaxError, which gets the 1-based line number as
   * `line`. `'skip'` leaves the line out and passes the error to `onError`.
   */
  errors?: 'throw' | 'skip';
  /** Called with each skipped line's error and its line number, with `errors: 'skip'`. */
  onError?: (error: Error & { line: number }, line: number) => void;
}

/**
 * A TransformStream from text or bytes with one polyline per line (\n or
 * \r\n) to one result per line: its points, or with `field` the line's JSON
 * object with that field decoded. Blank lines are skipped, and a line can be
 * split between chunks anywhere.
 */
export class DecodeLinesStream extends TransformStream<Chunk, any> {
  /** Takes the options decode takes, plus `flat`, `field`, `errors` and `onError`. */
  constructor(options?: LinesOptions | number);
}

/**
 * A TransformStream from one line's points per chunk (or with `field`, an
 * object whose field holds them) to one line of text: the polyline, or the
 * object as JSON with the field encoded, and a \n.
 */
export class EncodeLinesStream extends TransformStream<any, string> {
  /** Takes the options encode takes, plus `flat`, `field`, `errors` and `onError`. */
  constructor(options?: LinesOptions | number);
}

/** Anything `for await` reads, or a ReadableStream (read with a reader where it isn't async iterable, as in older Safari versions). */
export type Source<T> = AsyncIterable<T> | Iterable<T> | ReadableStream<T>;

/**
 * Yields the points of one polyline read from chunks of text or bytes: a
 * fetch body, a Node Readable, an async generator. One point at a time;
 * DecodeStream and PolylineDecoder give whole batches, which is faster.
 *
 * ```js
 * for await (const [lat, lng] of decodeIterable(fs.createReadStream('route.txt'))) { ... }
 * ```
 */
export function decodeIterable(chunks: Source<Chunk> | Chunk, options?: OptionsArg): AsyncGenerator<Point, void, undefined>;

/**
 * Yields the polyline for points (or arrays of points) from any source, in
 * pieces of about 64 KB. For a piece per input as soon as it arrives, use
 * PolylineEncoder or EncodeStream.
 */
export function encodeIterable<O extends StreamOptions | number = TupleOptions>(points: Source<O extends FlatOptions ? ArrayLike<number> : PointsChunk>, options?: O): AsyncGenerator<string, void, undefined>;

/** Yields one result per line of text or bytes, like DecodeLinesStream. */
export function decodeLines(chunks: Source<Chunk> | Chunk, options?: LinesOptions | number): AsyncGenerator<any, void, undefined>;

/** Yields one line of text per array of points (or object, with `field`), like EncodeLinesStream. */
export function encodeLines(items: Source<any>, options?: LinesOptions | number): AsyncGenerator<string, void, undefined>;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/google`

Google Maps JavaScript API helpers: decodePath and encodePath with the
signatures of google.maps.geometry.encoding, without loading the geometry
library.

```js
import { decodePath } from '@duoquote/polytini/google';
new google.maps.Polyline({ path: decodePath(route.polyline.encodedPolyline), map });
```

On JSR this entry is typed by `types/google.jsr.d.ts`, a copy with structural types, because JSR builds its docs without node_modules.

`types/google.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/google, using the google.maps types from
// @types/google.maps. Those are global declarations, not a module, so they
// are pulled in with a reference directive: types only, nothing at runtime.
/// <reference types="google.maps" />
import type * as P from './index.d.ts';
import type { Options, Point } from './index.d.ts';

export declare const PolylineError: typeof P.PolylineError;
export type PolylineError = P.PolylineError;

/** A LatLng constructor: google.maps.LatLng or anything built the same way. */
export type LatLngConstructor = new (lat: number, lng: number, noClampNoWrap?: boolean) => google.maps.LatLng;

export interface DecodePathOptions extends Omit<Options, 'order'> {
  /**
   * The class to build points with. Default: globalThis.google.maps.LatLng
   * when it exists. false or null returns LatLngLiteral objects.
   */
  LatLng?: LatLngConstructor | false | null;
  /** Passed to the LatLng constructor. Without it, LatLng clamps latitude and wraps longitude into [-180, 180). */
  noClampNoWrap?: boolean;
}

/** A point encodePath takes: google.maps.LatLng, LatLngLiteral or a [lat, lng] tuple. */
export type PathPoint = google.maps.LatLng | google.maps.LatLngLiteral | Point;

/**
 * Decodes an encoded path to LatLngLiteral objects (`LatLng: false`).
 */
export function decodePath(encodedPath: string, options: DecodePathOptions & { LatLng: false | null }): google.maps.LatLngLiteral[];
/**
 * Decodes an encoded path, like google.maps.geometry.encoding.decodePath,
 * to google.maps.LatLng objects. Without a `LatLng` option this uses
 * globalThis.google.maps.LatLng; when the Maps JavaScript API isn't loaded
 * the result is LatLngLiteral objects at runtime, so pass `LatLng: false`
 * there to get that type. Strict by default: a malformed string throws a
 * PolylineError unless `strict: false`.
 */
export function decodePath(encodedPath: string, options?: number | (DecodePathOptions & { LatLng?: LatLngConstructor })): google.maps.LatLng[];
export function decodePath(encodedPath: string, options?: number | DecodePathOptions): google.maps.LatLng[] | google.maps.LatLngLiteral[];

/**
 * Encodes a path, like google.maps.geometry.encoding.encodePath: an array or
 * MVCArray of google.maps.LatLng, LatLngLiteral or [lat, lng] tuples, mixed
 * or not. Precision 5 by default. `order: 'lnglat'` applies to tuples and
 * LatLng objects; literals are read by name. Strict by default.
 */
export function encodePath(path: readonly PathPoint[] | google.maps.MVCArray<PathPoint>, options?: number | Options): string;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/maplibre`

MapLibre GL JS: encoded polylines as GeoJSON sources and line layers. It
only calls addSource, addLayer and getSource on the map you pass.

```js
import { addPolylineLayer } from '@duoquote/polytini/maplibre';
map.on('load', () => addPolylineLayer(map, 'route', route.geometry, { precision: 6 }));
```

On JSR this entry is typed by `types/maplibre.jsr.d.ts`, a copy with structural types, because JSR builds its docs without node_modules.

`types/maplibre.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/maplibre, built from maplibre-gl's own types
// (type-only imports, so nothing is loaded at runtime). The source and layer
// types are taken from Map#addSource and Map#addLayer, so they follow the
// installed maplibre-gl version.
import type { Map, GeoJSONSource } from 'maplibre-gl';
import type { FeatureCollection, LineString, GeoJsonProperties } from 'geojson';
import type { Options } from './index.d.ts';

/** MapLibre's GeoJSON source specification. */
export type GeoJSONSourceSpecification = Extract<Parameters<Map['addSource']>[1], { type: 'geojson' }>;

/** MapLibre's line layer specification. */
export type LineLayerSpecification = Extract<Parameters<Map['addLayer']>[0], { type: 'line' }>;

export type FeatureId = string | number;

export interface DataOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends Options {
  /** Properties for every line, or an array with one object per line. Default {}. */
  properties?: P | P[];
  /** Feature id for every line, or an array with one per line. MapLibre's feature state needs numeric ids or promoteId. */
  id?: FeatureId | FeatureId[];
  /** Add a [west, south, east, north] bbox to each feature. Default false. */
  bbox?: boolean;
}

export interface SourceOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends DataOptions<P> {
  /** Other source options: lineMetrics, tolerance, promoteId, generateId, attribution, and so on. */
  source?: Partial<Omit<GeoJSONSourceSpecification, 'type' | 'data'>>;
}

export interface LayerOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends SourceOptions<P> {
  /** Merged into the line layer: paint, layout, filter, minzoom, maxzoom, metadata, or another id. */
  layer?: Partial<Omit<LineLayerSpecification, 'type' | 'source'>>;
  /** The id of an existing layer to insert the new layer before. */
  beforeId?: string;
}

/** A GeoJSON source specification whose data is a FeatureCollection of LineStrings. */
export type PolylineSource<P = GeoJsonProperties> = GeoJSONSourceSpecification & {
  type: 'geojson';
  data: FeatureCollection<LineString, P>;
};

/** A FeatureCollection<LineString> ([lng, lat]) with one Feature per encoded string. */
export function polylineData<P = GeoJsonProperties>(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | DataOptions<P>): FeatureCollection<LineString, P>;

/** `{ type: 'geojson', data }` for map.addSource or a style's sources. */
export function polylineSource<P = GeoJsonProperties>(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | SourceOptions<P>): PolylineSource<P>;

/** Adds a GeoJSON source and a line layer, both named `id`. Returns the map. */
export function addPolylineLayer<M extends Map, P = GeoJsonProperties>(map: M, id: string, encoded: string | string[], options?: number | LayerOptions<P>): M;

/** Replaces the data of the GeoJSON source `id`. Returns setData's Promise. Throws a PolylineError if there is no such GeoJSON source. */
export function setPolylineData<P = GeoJsonProperties>(map: Map, id: string, encoded: string | string[], options?: number | DataOptions<P>): ReturnType<GeoJSONSource['setData']>;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/mapbox`

Mapbox GL JS 3: the same functions as `/maplibre`, which make the same
calls on a Mapbox map.

```js
import { addPolylineLayer } from '@duoquote/polytini/mapbox';
map.on('load', () => addPolylineLayer(map, 'route', encoded));
```

On JSR this entry is typed by `types/mapbox.jsr.d.ts`, a copy with structural types, because JSR builds its docs without node_modules.

`types/mapbox.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/mapbox: the same functions as the maplibre
// module, typed with mapbox-gl's own types (type-only imports). mapbox-gl's
// types use the GeoJSON namespace from @types/geojson.
import type { Map, GeoJSONSource, GeoJSONSourceSpecification, LineLayerSpecification } from 'mapbox-gl';
import type { FeatureCollection, LineString, GeoJsonProperties } from 'geojson';
import type { Options } from './index.d.ts';

export type { GeoJSONSourceSpecification, LineLayerSpecification };

// Repeated from maplibre.d.ts so this file does not need maplibre-gl installed.
export type FeatureId = string | number;

export interface DataOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends Options {
  /** Properties for every line, or an array with one object per line. Default {}. */
  properties?: P | P[];
  /** Feature id for every line, or an array with one per line. Feature state needs numeric ids or promoteId. */
  id?: FeatureId | FeatureId[];
  /** Add a [west, south, east, north] bbox to each feature. Default false. */
  bbox?: boolean;
}

export interface SourceOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends DataOptions<P> {
  /** Other source options: lineMetrics, tolerance, promoteId, generateId, attribution, and so on. */
  source?: Partial<Omit<GeoJSONSourceSpecification, 'type' | 'data'>>;
}

export interface LayerOptions<P = GeoJsonProperties> extends SourceOptions<P> {
  /** Merged into the line layer: paint, layout, filter, slot, minzoom, maxzoom, or another id. */
  layer?: Partial<Omit<LineLayerSpecification, 'type' | 'source'>>;
  /** The id of an existing layer to insert the new layer before. */
  beforeId?: string;
}

/** A GeoJSON source specification whose data is a FeatureCollection of LineStrings. */
export type PolylineSource<P = GeoJsonProperties> = GeoJSONSourceSpecification & {
  type: 'geojson';
  data: FeatureCollection<LineString, P>;
};

/** A FeatureCollection<LineString> ([lng, lat]) with one Feature per encoded string. */
export function polylineData<P = GeoJsonProperties>(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | DataOptions<P>): FeatureCollection<LineString, P>;

/** `{ type: 'geojson', data }` for map.addSource or a style's sources. */
export function polylineSource<P = GeoJsonProperties>(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | SourceOptions<P>): PolylineSource<P>;

/** Adds a GeoJSON source and a line layer, both named `id`. Returns the map. */
export function addPolylineLayer<M extends Map, P = GeoJsonProperties>(map: M, id: string, encoded: string | string[], options?: number | LayerOptions<P>): M;

/** Replaces the data of the GeoJSON source `id`. Returns what setData returns (the source). Throws a PolylineError if there is no such GeoJSON source. */
export function setPolylineData<P = GeoJsonProperties>(map: Map, id: string, encoded: string | string[], options?: number | DataOptions<P>): ReturnType<GeoJSONSource['setData']>;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/deckgl`

deck.gl: encoded polylines straight into deck.gl's binary data format,
for PathLayer, TripsLayer and SolidPolygonLayer. No deck.gl code is imported.

```js
import { binaryPaths } from '@duoquote/polytini/deckgl';
const data = binaryPaths(routes.map((r) => r.geometry), { precision: 6 });
new PathLayer({ id: 'routes', data, _pathType: 'open', getWidth: 3 });
```

`types/deckgl.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/deckgl. The results are plain objects in
// deck.gl's binary data shape, so they need no deck.gl types: they can be
// passed as `data` to PathLayer, TripsLayer and SolidPolygonLayer.

import type { Options } from './index.d.ts';

/** Options for binaryPolygons: polytini's options plus float32. */
export interface BinaryOptions extends Options {
  /** Float32Array instead of Float64Array. Smaller, and enough for most maps; deck.gl uses 64-bit positions only when given them. Default false. */
  float32?: boolean;
}

/** Options for binaryPaths: BinaryOptions plus timestamps. */
export interface PathOptions extends BinaryOptions {
  /**
   * For TripsLayer: the last value of each point (with dimensions 3 or 4) goes
   * to attributes.getTimestamps instead of the positions. The values are
   * divided by zFactor, like any value after the second, and always come out
   * as a Float32Array, because TripsLayer's timestamp attribute is 32-bit
   * (deck.gl 9.4 drew nothing given Float64Array timestamps). Default false.
   */
  timestamps?: boolean;
}

/** A deck.gl binary attribute. */
export interface BinaryAttribute<T extends Float32Array | Float64Array = Float32Array | Float64Array, S extends number = number> {
  /** The values, size per vertex. */
  value: T;
  /** Values per vertex. */
  size: S;
}

/** What binaryPaths returns: `data` for PathLayer or TripsLayer. */
export interface BinaryPaths<T extends Float32Array | Float64Array = Float32Array | Float64Array> {
  /** The number of paths, one per string. */
  length: number;
  /** The first vertex of each path, plus the vertex count at the end (length + 1 entries). */
  startIndices: Uint32Array;
  /** The vertex attributes. */
  attributes: {
    /** [lng, lat] (size 2) or [lng, lat, z] (size 3) per vertex. */
    getPath: BinaryAttribute<T, 2 | 3>;
    /** One value per vertex, with the timestamps option. Always 32-bit. */
    getTimestamps?: BinaryAttribute<Float32Array, 1>;
  };
}

/** What binaryPolygons returns: `data` for SolidPolygonLayer. */
export interface BinaryPolygons<T extends Float32Array | Float64Array = Float32Array | Float64Array> {
  /** The number of polygons, one ring per string. */
  length: number;
  /** The first vertex of each ring, plus the vertex count at the end (length + 1 entries). */
  startIndices: Uint32Array;
  /** The vertex attributes. */
  attributes: {
    /** [lng, lat] (size 2) or [lng, lat, z] (size 3) per vertex, every ring closed. */
    getPolygon: BinaryAttribute<T, 2 | 3>;
  };
}

/** Binary data for PathLayer and TripsLayer, one path per string. Pass _pathType: 'open' to skip deck.gl's normalization. */
export function binaryPaths(encoded: string | string[], options: PathOptions & { float32: true }): BinaryPaths<Float32Array>;
/** binaryPaths with Float64Array positions, the default. */
export function binaryPaths(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | (PathOptions & { float32?: false })): BinaryPaths<Float64Array>;
/** binaryPaths when float32 isn't known until runtime. */
export function binaryPaths(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | PathOptions): BinaryPaths;

/** Binary data for SolidPolygonLayer, one closed ring per string (no holes). */
export function binaryPolygons(encoded: string | string[], options: BinaryOptions & { float32: true }): BinaryPolygons<Float32Array>;
/** binaryPolygons with Float64Array positions, the default. */
export function binaryPolygons(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | (BinaryOptions & { float32?: false })): BinaryPolygons<Float64Array>;
/** binaryPolygons when float32 isn't known until runtime. */
export function binaryPolygons(encoded: string | string[], options?: number | BinaryOptions): BinaryPolygons;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/leaflet/auto`

Side-effect import that installs the Leaflet plugin on the global `L` that
Leaflet's UMD build sets. For ES module imports of Leaflet, use install(L)
from `/leaflet`.

```js
import '@duoquote/polytini/leaflet/auto';
```

On JSR this entry is typed by `types/leaflet-auto.jsr.d.ts`, a copy with structural types, because JSR builds its docs without node_modules.

`types/leaflet-auto.d.ts`:

// Side-effect import that patches the global L. The added methods are
// typed in leaflet.d.ts.
/// <reference path="./leaflet.d.ts" />

```

### `@duoquote/polytini/openlayers`

OpenLayers: a faster drop-in for ol/format/Polyline. You pass ol's
classes in, so polytini doesn't import ol.

```js
import Polyline from 'ol/format/Polyline.js';
import LineString from 'ol/geom/LineString.js';
import { createPolylineFormat } from '@duoquote/polytini/openlayers';
const format = new (createPolylineFormat({ Polyline, LineString }))({ factor: 1e6 });
```

On JSR this entry is typed by `types/openlayers.jsr.d.ts`, a copy with structural types, because JSR builds its docs without node_modules.

`types/openlayers.d.ts`:

```ts
// Types for @duoquote/polytini/openlayers. Type-only imports: nothing from
// ol is loaded at runtime, you pass its classes to createPolylineFormat.
import type OlPolyline from 'ol/format/Polyline.js';
import type { Options } from 'ol/format/Polyline.js';
import type OlLineString from 'ol/geom/LineString.js';

export type { Options };

/** ol's classes, as imported from ol/format/Polyline.js and ol/geom/LineString.js. */
export interface OpenLayersClasses {
  Polyline: typeof OlPolyline;
  LineString: typeof OlLineString;
}

/**
 * Makes a drop-in for ol/format/Polyline: the same constructor options
 * (factor, geometryLayout), methods and output, faster. Unlike ol's,
 * writeGeometry never changes the geometry it is given. Also takes the `ol`
 * namespace of the full build ({ format: { Polyline }, geom: { LineString } }).
 */
export function createPolylineFormat(
  ol: OpenLayersClasses | { format: { Polyline: typeof OlPolyline }; geom: { LineString: typeof OlLineString } },
): typeof OlPolyline;
```

### `@duoquote/polytini/cli`

```

JSR only. On npm, the same command is the `polytini` bin.

`types/cli.d.ts`:
